title: Close-area relocalization after VIO loss: scan-to-map pose hypotheses, ratio + persistence acceptance, hover until one wins
summary: Relocalizer for the close-area arena. After a detected VIO loss (reset_counter change, quality 0, or a scan-to-map innovation test) a pose source that wraps the arena's VIO-like estimator reports quality 0 (a planner gate hovers), matches the 72-beam range scan against the known 0.1 m occupancy grid by correlative grid search on a likelihood field (EDT distance, sigma 0.10 m, +-2 m window), keeps up to 5 hypotheses 0.5 m apart, and accepts one with a named rule: best score >= 0.6, best >= 1.02 x second, and the same winner for 3 scans; 'none of them' keeps hovering and widens the window to +-4 m. On accept it re-anchors the estimate. experiment.py flies the arena's A* known-map planner on 100 random layouts under the dropout and jump faults and compares no relocalization, hover only, single-hypothesis commit at once, and the multi-hypothesis rule, with ablations without the innovation test, plus a symmetric 2 m x 14.8 m corridor where shifted poses look the same. Thresholds set on seed-1 static poses (tune.py). Synthetic arena only.
verified: ran 2026-11-09 with CPython 3.12.10 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 on an Apple M3 Max, in the sample venv: experiment.py --layouts 100 --seed 0 ran twice with identical tables (wall 70.7 s on 8 workers for the kept run); experiment.py --corridor --runs 20 ran once (21.3 s); tune.py on seed 1 wrote results/tune_seed1.json. Every number in README is from results/. test_smoke.py: 1 passed in the venv, 1 skipped under plain python3 without numpy. No arena file was edited. Layouts, vehicle, estimator and range sensor are simulated; yaw is truth; the map is the exact prior grid; no SITL, no real drone or lidar.
shows: What the drone does when VIO is lost indoors: scan-to-map relocalization with up to 5 hypotheses and a ratio + persistence rule vs commit-at-once vs no relocalization, under dropout and jump faults, plus a symmetric corridor
runtime: ~71 s for 100 layouts x 2 faults x 7 arms on 8 workers; corridor ~21 s
key_result: [100 random layouts, seed 0, A* known map](README.md#results-ran-2026-11-09-apple-m3-max-cpython-31210-numpy-254-scipy-1181): no relocalization reached 64 % (dropout) / 36 % (jump) with 1 % / 9 % collisions; commit-at-once relocalization 100 % / 100 %, 0 % collisions, 2 / 4 wrong commits all later corrected; the multi-hypothesis rule 80 % / 93 %, 0 wrong commits, but hovers until stuck when the scan has under 10 returns or two poses tie; in a symmetric corridor it hovers in 20 of 20 runs
